label: streaming table vs materialized view
title: Streaming table vs materialized view: late updates need a materialized view
definition: A streaming table processes each input row once and expects an append-only source. A materialized view stores results and recalculates them on each refresh, including updates and deletes in the source. A regular view stores no data and runs its query on every read.
points: A10 exam-style question: Nov 2, TX shows 58.50. On Nov 4 a late update changes order 5002 (a Nov 2 order) from 30.00 to 36.00. Which object keeps Nov 2 right? Answer: B, a materialized view (64.50 after its next refresh, expected).
The trap: a streaming read of a Delta table fails on UPDATE, DELETE or MERGE. With skipChangeCommits the change is skipped. The old day stays wrong until a full refresh.
Checklist: latency, refresh (manual, scheduled, on update), late data (old rows change: materialized view), cost (a view runs the full query on every read).
Free Edition: one active pipeline per pipeline type.
example_note: A10 example. Expected behavior from the Databricks docs; view and snapshot results checked on local Apache Spark 4.0, not on Databricks.
code:
CREATE OR REPLACE MATERIALIZED VIEW gold.daily_sales_by_region
  SCHEDULE EVERY 1 HOUR
AS SELECT o.order_date, c.state AS region,
  COUNT(*) AS order_count, SUM(o.amount) AS total_sales
FROM silver.orders o JOIN silver.customers c
  ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY o.order_date, c.state;
misconception: Streaming does not mean fresher for every case. A streaming table does not go back and fix a day it already processed.
memory_trick: Streaming tables read each row once. Materialized views recompute the answer.
remember: Ingest append-only data: streaming table. Gold aggregates with late updates: materialized view. Light ad hoc slices: view.
